shapes.note: sparse MLA prefill: q[M,64,576] bf16 attends its per-query top-2048 rows of kv[32768,576] bf16 -> out[M,64,512] bf16, sm_scale=576**-0.5=1/24, seed 0. First 512 dims = value/latent, last 64 = rope; QK spans all 576, PV/out use only the first 512. Unified S/KV=32768 (DEC-4).

approaches.summary: Purpose-built native-64-head Triton flash sparse-MLA prefill kernel replacing the passthrough. One program = one query row x 64 heads: single-pass fp32 online softmax over the per-query top-2048 keys, QK as bf16xbf16->fp32 MFMA over all 576 dims, PV as fp32-accumulated bf16 MFMA over the first 512 dims, bf16 output, no intermediate HBM. The decisive lever is matrix_instr_nonkdim=16: Triton's default MFMA selection (32x32x8) for this skinny-M (64-head) dot is ~40% slower than forcing the 16x16x16 instruction (pure scheduling, identical math). Winner launch config BH64/BK64/num_warps4/num_stages1/waves_per_eu1/bf16-PV/mfma16/kpack0. Does HALF the FLOPs of the padded-128 ASM baseline; falls back to the untouched reference on any shape/dtype/arch surprise (never load-bearing).
approaches.why: The ASM baseline pads 64->128 heads (~2x FLOPs) because gfx942 has no native bf16 gqa=64 MLA kernel; a native-64 kernel does half the compute. An index-locality probe showed the ASM path is compute/padding-bound not gather-bound (collapsing the gather to one cached row saves only ~15%), so the native-64 kernel has real headroom. matrix_instr_nonkdim=16 is the ~40% lever that turns a trending-NO-GO (default MFMA, 4-12% short of ASM) into a 3/3 win.

lesson: For GLM-5.2 DSA sparse-MLA prefill on gfx942 (q[M,64,576] bf16, per-query top-2048 of kv[32768,576] bf16), the aiter reference dispatches to ASM mla_decode_fwd which pads q 64->128 heads (~2x wasted FLOPs) because gfx942 has no native bf16 gqa=64 MLA kernel. A purpose-built native-64-head Triton flash kernel (fp32 online softmax, bf16xbf16->fp32 QK MFMA over all 576 dims, fp32-accumulated bf16 PV over the first 512 dims) does half the compute and wins 3/3 (geo 1.33x, min cons 1.27x, worst calc_diff 1.87e-6). The decisive ~40% lever is matrix_instr_nonkdim=16: Triton's default 32x32x8 MFMA is wrong for the skinny-M 64-head dot; forcing the 16x16x16 instruction is pure scheduling (identical math, calc_diff unchanged). The win is STRUCTURAL (fewer FLOPs), not higher per-useful-FLOP efficiency (native-64 MFU ~20% vs ASM's real ~30%) -- ACCEPT and do not push. Keep QK/softmax/output-accumulator fp32; BK power-of-2 (64 best); num_stages=1 (ns=2 OOMs the 64KB LDS at BK64).
transfers_to: any skinny-M (few-head) MLA/attention tl.dot on gfx942 where Triton's default 32x32x8 MFMA under-uses the matrix core -- force matrix_instr_nonkdim=16 (16x16x16) as a pure-scheduling knob

sparse-MLA / GQA prefill where the vendor path pads a small head count up to a supported tile -- a native-head-count Triton flash kernel wins by halving the padded FLOPs, not by out-MFU-ing the vendor kernel
caveats: The win is structural (half the FLOPs of the padded ASM baseline), NOT higher per-useful-FLOP efficiency: native-64 MFU ~20% vs the ASM baseline's real ~30% per-useful-FLOP. Codex (task7) reviewed and returned ACCEPT / do-not-push-higher; no low-risk lever remains after the full knob sweep.

bf16 PV (fp32 accumulator) is gate-safe HERE (worst calc_diff 1.87e-6, elementwise_failed 0 every shape) because prefill M is large; the sibling decode kernel kept fp32 PV opt-in-only for its tiny-M near-zero output elems. QK / online-softmax state / output accumulator MUST stay fp32.
BK must be a power of 2 (Triton block-dim constraint); BK=48 fails to compile. BK=64 num_stages=2 double-buffering OOMs the 64KB LDS (KV tile [64,576] bf16 ~72KB); num_stages=1 fits and is faster.

At M=1024 the aiter ASM reference itself fails the fully-f32 math oracle (calc_diff 5.44e-6 > 5e-6), so a fallback-to-reference at M=1024 would score INCORRECT -- the Triton path must (and does) succeed there; the fallback is a genuine-error safety net only.
Op-level GATE-1 result only; e2e/GATE-2 out of scope (dsa is off the e2e prefill hot path and the node lacks a legal TP config -- PLAN DEC-1).
